title: Congress slams Modi government over CBI counsel’s ‘no-show’ in fast-track court in paper leak case
author: PTI
content_html:
The Congress on Monday (July 27, 2026) asked with what face the Narendra Modi government is "tom-toming" fast-track courts as a solution to the paper leaks crisis when its own CBI "failed to dispatch" a legal representative to the inaugural hearing of the fast-track court in such a case.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the Delhi High Court set up a Special Fast Track Court in Delhi's Rouse Avenue complex on July 23 to hear the NEET-UG 2026 Paper leak case.

"Tellingly, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) failed to dispatch a legal representative to the inaugural hearing of this fast track court. It forced an immediate adjournment of the case," Mr. Ramesh said on X.

"With what face is the Modi Government tom-toming fast-track courts as a solution to the crisis of paper-leaks? Its own CBI is showing zero initiative in investigating and prosecuting these cases," he said.

Mr. Ramesh's remarks came after the Special Fast Track Court at Delhi's Rouse Avenue Courts on Monday (July 27, 2026) directed the director of prosecution to appoint a public prosecutor to represent the State (CBI) in the NEET UG 2026 paper leak case. The direction came after no one appeared on behalf of the CBI during the hearing.

The Delhi High Court last Thursday (July 23, 2026) notified a designated court to deal with criminal cases arising from paper leaks as well as the use of other unfair means in public examinations.

The move came after Prime Minister Narendra Modi — in the wake of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protests here at Jantar Mantar demanding, among other things, reforms in the education system and resignation of then education minister Dharmandra Pradhan — announced that fast-track courts would be set up to swiftly deal with cases of paper leaks.

The CJP called off the protest on July 25 after Mr. Pradhan resigned and the government accepted other demands of the newly formed organisation.

In a notification, the High Court administration said judicial officer Anu Grover Baliga's court shall function as a "Specially Designated Fast Track Court" to try offences under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 and connected offences, with immediate effect.

Mr. Modi said the government decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks.

He said he has directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps on the issue of paper leaks.

title: BJP plans nationwide campaign to mark Guru Ravidas’ birth anniversary
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday (July 27, 2026) said it would launch a nationwide ‘Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyan’ (campaign for social harmony and resolve) from July 29, 2026, to February 20, 2027, to mark the 650th birth anniversary of the mystic poet-saint Guru Ravidas.

Also read: Guru Ravidas, the reformer

At a press conference held by BJP national general secretaries Tarun Chugh and Dushyant Kumar Gautam, the party said 131 sacred urns would be sent across the country from Varanasi, the birthplace of Ravidas.

Initiatives for social harmony would be organised at 21,000 locations; a festival of lights would be organised at 51,000 temples; an outreach campaign would be carried out with saints, students, temples, hostels, and religious groups; and processions, including a month-long yatra from Jalandhar to Varanasi, would be taken out in different parts of the country, they said.

The Narendra Modi government had undertaken several initiatives to preserve the saint’s legacy, including the development of airports, special trains, his birthplace, pilgrim routes, and the restoration of several sites linked to Ravidas, the BJP leaders said.

The birth anniversary campaign’s objective was to take the message of social harmony, equality, and public awakening as preached by Ravidas, Mr. Chugh said. Ravidas lived in an age when Sikandar Lodi, the Tughlaqs, and Timur were “engaged in carrying out religious conversions and demolishing temples across the country”, Mr. Gautam said.

“At that time, their only slogan was ‘the sword or the Quran’. During that mediaeval period, people had no means of expressing their views, and there was an atmosphere of widespread distress everywhere. At such a time, many great saints of the Bhakti movement, including Goswami Tulsidas, Kabir Das, Sant Tukaram, Guru Nanak, and Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, carried the knowledge and values preserved in Sanskrit to the masses through their respective regional languages, thereby creating public awareness and providing new direction to society throughout the country,” Mr. Gautam added.

“During that period, the contribution of Sant Guru Ravidas was extremely significant. It was for this reason that Kabir conferred upon him the title of ‘Sant Shiromani Guru Ravidas Ji’,” the BJP leader said.

Sant Ravidas’s vision for an egalitarian society about 650 years ago was far ahead of its time, Mr. Gautam said. Abraham Lincoln launched a movement against slavery in 1837, and B.R. Ambedkar, while drafting the Constitution, laid down the principles of equality, liberty, and fraternity, he said.

“However, long before them, Sant Guru Ravidas had already conveyed the message of ‘chhote-bade sab base’ (small and big live together). He envisioned a casteless society and ‘Beghampura’, a place where there is neither sorrow nor suffering,” the BJP spokesperson said.

title: Bombay High Court permits Nitin Gadkari to sue Meta, Google, X over ethanol-linked deepfake posts
author: Chinmay Gaikwad
content_html:
The Bombay High Court on Monday (July 27, 2026) allowed Union Minister Nitin Gadkari to initiate legal proceedings against Meta, Google, X and other unnamed entities over social media content that he alleged falsely links him to the Centre’s Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP).

Justice Abhay Ahuja, presiding over a single-judge Bench, granted Mr. Gadkari leave to file a substantive civil suit, seeking relief that includes the removal of the content in question from the internet.

The petition was moved under Clause XII of the Letters Patent. This procedural requirement necessitates the High Court’s permission when a part of the cause of action arises outside the High Court’s territorial jurisdiction. Mr. Gadkari also indicated his intention to approach the Supreme Court in the matter. A detailed order is awaited.

In the proposed suit, Mr. Gadkari outlined the background of the Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP), introduced by the Central government in 2003 as a national policy initiative for blending ethanol with petrol in phases. The implementation of 20% ethanol blending with petrol (E20) was achieved during the 2025-2026 period. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas looks after the EBP and has issued official press releases and clarifications on its progress.

Mr. Gadkari stated that although he has served as the Union Minister for Road Transport since 2014, he has no role in the E20 policy decisions. However, the Minister alleged that several social media posts, created and circulated by unknown users, falsely portray him as responsible for the EBP’s implementation.

The court filings noted that the posts “falsely, maliciously and without any basis whatsoever” allege that Mr. Gadkari and members of his family derived undue pecuniary benefits from the implementation of the EBP, thereby, inter alia, insinuating corruption, nepotism, conflict of interest, abuse of official position, misuse of governmental authority and other acts of impropriety.”

Mr. Gadkari identified at least 24 posts that he claims are defamatory and has sought directions for their removal. The Minister clarified that the suit is not intended to prevent public discussion or fair criticism of his decisions or official functions, adding, “The content in question is false and fabricated.”

The suit, which seeks damages of ₹11 crore, is expected to be listed before Justice Arif Doctor.

title: India summons Ukraine envoy, lodges protest over killing of Indian in attack on merchant vessel
author: PTI
content_html:
India summoned Ukrainian Ambassador Oleksandr Polishchuk on Monday (July 27, 2026) and lodged a strong protest over the killing of an Indian seafarer in an attack on a merchant vessel in the Black Sea last week.

The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said it conveyed to the envoy New Delhi's serious concern over the incident and condemned such attacks on commercial shipping in the strongest terms.

The vessel MV Omorfi reportedly came under Ukrainian drone strikes amid fresh hostilities between Russia and Ukraine.

"Today, the Ambassador of Ukraine to India, Oleksandr Polishchuk, was summoned to the Ministry of External Affairs in connection with the attack on the commercial vessel MV Omorfi which resulted in the tragic death of an Indian national," the MEA said.

"The Ministry conveyed its serious concern over the incident and condemned such attacks on commercial shipping in the strongest terms, underscoring their adverse impact on the safety of maritime navigation, freedom of navigation, and international commerce," it said in a statement.

It said the ambassador was "requested to convey to the Ukrainian authorities India's strong concerns over the targeting of commercial vessels and reiterated that such actions, which endanger the lives of innocent civilian seafarers, are unacceptable and must be avoided".

title: Fraudsters create fake website of Kumarakrupa Guest House to cheat guests; case booked
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Central CEN police have registered a case after unidentified persons allegedly created a fake website of the State government-run Kumarakrupa Guest House and cheated customers by accepting online payments for room bookings.

According to the complaint filed by Karthik Santhosh, senior manager of the guest house, unidentified persons created a fake website (https://kumarkrupaguesthouse.in/) by misusing the name of the guest house.

The police said the fraudsters allegedly offered online room bookings through the fake website and sent fabricated bills and invoices to customers, inducing them to make online payments. The scam came to light after several customers informed the guest house management that they had received fake booking confirmations and payment receipts.

Based on the complaint, the Central CEN Crime police have registered an FIR. The police are investigating the operators of the fake website, tracing the digital trail, financial transactions and other electronic evidence to identify those behind the fraud.

Sources in the government clarified that neither can members of the public book rooms paying money in the Kumarakrupa Guest House, nor do they have a website.

Not the first time

This is not the first time people have been cheated with fake bookings for rooms in the the government-run guest house.

In June this year, a politician from Bijapur allegedly cheated of ₹99,666 by cyberfraudsters while attempting to book accommodation at the guest house through an online platform. In September 2025, a Punjab sessions court judge, who was visiting Bengaluru, was duped of ₹12,000 after a staff member in the Criminal Investigation Department shared a fake contact number sourced from Google. The personal assistant of a senior police officer, instead of checking with the government guest house directly, searched online and passed on a number that turned out to be fraudulent.

title: Govt. gives nod to acquire land to lay new broad gauge railway line between Mannargudi and Pattukottai
author: R Rajaram
content_html:
The Tamil Nadu government has accorded administrative sanction for the acquisition of land in connection with the construction of the long-pending new broad gauge railway line between Mannargudi and Pattukottai in Tiruchi Railway Division limits.

The move gives a thrust to the 41-km railway line project, which has remained on paper for nearly 14 years after its announcement by the Railway Ministry in 2012.  An order according sanction for the acquisition of private and government poromboke land was issued a few days ago based on the proposal of the District Collectors of Thanjavur and Tiruvarur and the recommendation of the Commissioner of Land Administrative Reforms. A copy of the government order has been forwarded to the Chief Engineer, Construction, Southern Railway.

The government has sanctioned the creation of 13 posts of special staff each in Thanjavur and Tiruvarur districts for the land acquisition work in Thanjavur and Tiruvarur districts.

Wet, dry, manavari and government poromboke lands are to be acquired in the two districts.  In Thanjavur district, 89.49 hectares of patta lands and 17.63 hectares of government poromboke lands in Nadiyammalpuram and 14 other villages in Pattukottai taluk are to be acquired.

Officials appointed

In Tiruvarur district, 87.53 hectares of patta lands and 8.92 hectares of government poromboke lands in Ramapuram and 14 other villages in Mannargudi taluk are to be acquired under the Tamil Nadu Acquisition of Land for Industrial Purposes Act.  The District Revenue Officers of Thanjavur and Tiruvarur have been appointed as Land Acquisition Officers in their respective districts.

“The Mannargudi-Pattukottai BG line project was announced in 2012-13 by the Railway Ministry during the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance regime.  It was brought as an extension of the Mayiladuthurai-Tiruvarur-Karaikudi and Thiruthuraipoondi-Agasthiyampalli gauge conversion projects. Tenders were initially floated for the construction of a bridge across Bamini river in Tiruvarur district. The bridge work started with construction of a few pillars and subsequently stopped. The bridge work across Kannanaru and Nasuvani river never took off and the project remained only on paper due to delay in land acquisition,” said D. Manoharan, a former railway employee and a former office-bearer of a trade union based in Mannargudi.

Cost escalation

The estimated cost of the project was initially pegged at over ₹200 crore but now it had risen by over 300%, said Mr. Manoharan. Vexed over the inordinate delay in its implementation, various associations staged a rally in Mannargudi a couple of days ago demanding early implementation of the project which will have two block railway stations enroute: Paravakottai and Madukkur.

“The sanction for land acquisition after a long time is a definitely welcome move as it would finally give a big push to the project which has faced inordinate delay. The railway administration should no longer delay releasing funds and sanction at least ₹50 crore initially towards payment for land acquisition so that the project takes off,” said Mr. Manoharan.  The project once implemented would enhance rail connectivity not only in the delta region but also in the southern districts, he added.

title: Yathindra urges supporters to respect Siddaramaiah’s decision to quit electoral politics
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Urban Development Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah said there is a need for supporters of former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah to respect his decision to retire from electoral politics.

Fielding queries from reporters in Mysuru on Monday, Mr. Yathindra, who is Mr. Siddaramaiah’s son, said his father had been maintaining that he would not be contesting the Assembly elections of 2028.  “He had said it earlier also and repeated it when he was the Chief Minister too,” he said while pointing to the need for his supporters to respect Mr. Siddaramaiah’s decision to stay out of electoral politics.

Referring to the possible pressure from his supporters to contest elections again, Mr. Yathindra said Mr. Siddaramaiah has made it clear that he will remain in active politics even if he quits electoral politics. “He will continue to raise voice for the vulnerable people in the society,” he said.

When pressed further, Mr. Yathindra said his father’s health and well-being were more important than persuading him to contest another election.

While making it clear that he, as a son, would not try to convince his father to reconsider his decision, Mr. Yathindra said his father was almost 80 years old now. “I think he should give attention to his health and not neglect it due to his work. So, I will not ask him to change his decision,” he said.

He said Siddaramaiah was a man who stood by his decisions and did not change them. “When he makes a firm decision, nobody can change it,” he said.

Kambala in Mysuru Dasara

Commenting on the proposal to organise Kambala as part of this year’s Mysuru Dasara festivities, he clarified that no final decision had been taken. “We have only been asked to make the necessary preparations. It has not yet been decided that Kambala will definitely be held,” he said.

KSPC scams

On the alleged scams by Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), Mr. Yathindra said the KPSC Chairman Shivashankarappa S. Sahukar had been appointed during the previous BJP government’s tenure and that the State government did not have the authority to remove him. However, the Chairman had since been suspended by the Governor.

Mr. Yathindra, meanwhile, alleged that the suspended Chairman is represented by lawyers of “RSS and BJP” in the court and accused the BJP, which is criticising the scams in KPSC, of adopting double standards by taking such contradictory positions.

Reacting to demands for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, Mr. Yathindra alleged that the Centre had so far displayed an attitude of refusing to admit mistakes, but had now yielded to sustained student protests. He said the Union government should abandon what he described as its belief that people would accept whatever decisions it took.

Urban Development Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah said there is a need for supporters of former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah to respect his decision to retire from electoral politics.
Fielding queries from reporters in Mysuru on Monday, Mr. Yathindra, who is Mr. Siddaramaiah’s son, said his father had been maintaining that he would not be contesting the Assembly elections of 2028.  “He had said it earlier also and repeated it when he was the Chief Minister too,” he said while pointing to the need for his supporters to respect Mr. Siddaramaiah’s decision to stay out of electoral politics.
Referring to the possible pressure from his supporters to contest elections again, Mr. Yathindra said Mr. Siddaramaiah has made it clear that he will remain in active politics even if he quits electoral politics. “He will continue to raise voice for the vulnerable people in the society,” he said.
When pressed further, Mr. Yathindra said his father’s health and well-being were more important than persuading him to contest another election.
While making it clear that he, as a son, would not try to convince his father to reconsider his decision, Mr. Yathindra said his father was almost 80 years old now. “I think he should give attention to his health and not neglect it due to his work. So, I will not ask him to change his decision,” he said.
He said Siddaramaiah was a man who stood by his decisions and did not change them. “When he makes a firm decision, nobody can change it,” he said.
Kambala in Mysuru Dasara
Commenting on the proposal to organise Kambala as part of this year’s Mysuru Dasara festivities, he clarified that no final decision had been taken. “We have only been asked to make the necessary preparations. It has not yet been decided that Kambala will definitely be held,” he said.
KSPC scams
On the alleged scams by Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), Mr. Yathindra said the KPSC Chairman Shivashankarappa S. Sahukar had been appointed during the previous BJP government’s tenure and that the State government did not have the authority to remove him. However, the Chairman had since been suspended by the Governor.
Mr. Yathindra, meanwhile, alleged that the suspended Chairman is represented by lawyers of “RSS and BJP” in the court and accused the BJP, which is criticising the scams in KPSC, of adopting double standards by taking such contradictory positions.
